A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multimodal data-provenance audit. All 70 pages, including Appendices A–F, support comparison. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons locate differences only on pages 1 and 29.

before.justification: v1 reports original data-analysis results from a manual audit of 3,916 datasets, including sourcing trends, licensing restrictions, and geographical and linguistic representation (Table 1, Section 3, Appendices B–D).

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical audit and its quantitative results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The audit methodology, provenance-tracing procedure, restriction taxonomy, and annotation rules remain unchanged in Section 2 and Appendices B and D. No method component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both retain the same dataset and task coverage. Table 1 lists 3,717 text, 95 speech, and 104 video datasets in each version; the modality-specific selection scope and appendix inventories are unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing algorithms against a proposed model. The descriptive comparisons across modalities, sources, and time remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Dataset-selection criteria, annotation procedures, dataset-versus-collection aggregation, token/hour measurements, and Gini-based representation analyses are unchanged (Sections 2–3 and Appendix D).

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the same dataset-size and task-distribution analyses in Figures 6–7. No ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis, or case study is added, removed, or revised.

E5.justification: Both retain Figure 4's 95% confidence intervals for Gini coefficients and Section 3.3's significance discussion at p = 0.05. Statistical procedures and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and findings in Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–10 are unchanged. For example, Figure 3 retains geographical Gini coefficients of 0.92, 0.86, and 0.74 for text, speech, and video respectively.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised. The existing explanation and use of the Gini measure remain identical.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same novelty and contribution claims: a broad longitudinal multimodal audit, increasing web and synthetic sourcing, undocumented source restrictions, and persistent representational inequality.

C2.justification: Section 4 retains the same interpretations and limitations concerning privacy, copyright, creator-identity proxies, uncertain dataset usage, proprietary-data visibility, modality selection, and legal enforceability.

D1.justification: Annotation and aggregation details, dataset/license documentation, and code/data-release statements are unchanged. The PDFs also retain identical hyperlink destinations; no access instructions or reproducibility information are revised.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, Appendix A, and both bibliographies are unchanged. No cited work or substantive positioning relative to earlier research is added, removed, or revised.

P1.justification: Naana Obeng-Marnu moves earlier in the author order. Appendix E removes Vivek Sharma's video-dataset lead designation and Hanlin Li's senior-advisor credit. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; research prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The author block and contribution-credit bullets undergo local spacing and line-wrapping changes on pages 1 and 29. Figures, table structures, captions, and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 revises author order and contribution credits with minor text reflow, while preserving the scientific content, evidence, limitations, and reproducibility documentation. These edits establish no meaningful net change in the paper's overall research quality.
